To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) age is a significant variable in the perception of ambiguous figures, (2) age is not a significant variable in locating hidden figures, (3) education and verbal ability are significant variables in both ambiguous and hidden figure perception, and (4) living conditions are a significant variable in both ambiguous and embedded/hidden figure perception.
the elderly are less likely than young adults to see reversals and find embedded figures.
the elderly are less likely than the young to report seeing reversals of ambiguous figures, and they are less likely to find embedded/hidden figures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on perception and with the relationship of perceptual abilities to other psychological processes.
the effects of age, living conditions, and perceptual training on perceptual organization.
the effects of age and living conditions on perceptual functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
age is a factor, but that the effect is dependent upon the nature of the task and the nature of the subject's life history.
age and environment interact to influence the number of reversally reported figures, but not the number of embedded figures found.
the elderly are not perceptually impaired in general but that they do not have the intactness and competence of younger people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of age on perception are not simple, but rather are complex and interactive, depending on the task, the subject, and the method.
age is a factor, but not the only or most important one.
the older subjects' scores were lower than those of the young, but the difference was not great, and the difference between young and old in performance on the embedded figures task was small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of participants is an important variable to control for when studying visual perception.
the age of the subject and the environment in which they were tested are important factors to consider.
age is a significant variable to consider when interpreting performance on ambiguous figure tasks.
